body.x: Neowise, a Physical AI company led by CEO Donghyuk Shin, announced on Nov. 10 that its 3D digital twin platform NeoTwin has been named a CES Innovation Awards 2027 Honoree in the Construction & Industrial Tech category, in the awards program run by the Consumer Technology Association (CTA).

The CES Innovation Awards are presented each year to products submitted from around the world, judged on innovation, engineering and functionality, and design. According to Neowise, no major domestic or global competitor in drone- and robot-captured 3D digital twins for construction had previously received a CES Innovation Award; founded in April 2024, Neowise becomes the first company in the field to be honored, just two years and seven months after its founding.

NeoTwin converts 2D footage captured by drones, robots and handheld devices into a fast 3D model within 15 seconds, automatically finds and re-captures coverage gaps, and completes a precise 3D digital twin within an hour. Its core technology combines RTK satellite positioning, an optical ranging sensor and a camera in a single device, extending the outdoor coordinate system seamlessly into GPS-denied indoor and underground spaces. Unlike existing solutions that treat outdoor drone surveying and indoor 360-degree capture as separate workflows, it unifies a single site into a single dataset.

The finished twin is automatically compared against the BIM (Building Information Model) to quantify whether construction matches the design and how far work has progressed. It can also generate a BIM automatically from 2D drawings alone within a day, allowing an immediate response to design changes. Neowise has validated the technology at a multi-kilometer new industrial facility and at construction sites across Korea, and offers on-premises deployment for high-security sites where data cannot leave the premises. Together with a partner that supplies safety-management solutions to about 1,500 construction sites in Korea, the company is rolling out NeoTwin across construction sites nationwide.

body.cap: Donghyuk Shin, CEO of Neowise | Photo - AVING News

body.x: "I want to apply this technology not only to new construction and civil-engineering projects but also to closely understand structures that have already been built," said Donghyuk Shin, CEO of Neowise. "In disaster safety under climate change, if we build accurate 3D digital twins of bridges, tunnels, retaining walls and aging buildings and monitor how their condition changes moment to moment, I am convinced we can prevent major accidents." He added, "Even for facilities built 20 to 30 years ago with no surviving drawings, we can rebuild the drawings and the BIM from actual measurements, and the same technology applies to the high-precision 3D digital twins that precision industries such as semiconductor fabs and plants are now looking to adopt."

Alongside the award, Neowise announced its full-scale entry into the image-processing market with NeoSight, an AI ISP (AI image signal processing) technology. NeoSight processes RAW data straight from the image sensor on an NPU (neural processing unit), restoring low light, haze, blur and noise simultaneously with a single neural network. It renders scenes lit only by starlight as bright as day and has achieved real-time processing at Full HD (1080p) above 30 frames per second while running on the NPU.

In a side-by-side comparison under identical conditions with a low-light-specialized camera used by many drone and robot makers, the company said a general-purpose image sensor costing about one-tenth as much, paired with NeoSight, outperformed the product with the premium low-light sensor in brightness, color reproduction and detail by a wide margin. Conventional methods hit a limit because raising sensor sensitivity amplifies noise and washes out color, but NeoSight overcomes this by using AI to lift the faint brightness information still present in the raw data. "We have completely solved the problem of robot and drone vision getting lost in the dark," Shin said, noting that because it beats darkness with AI algorithms rather than expensive sensors, it can be layered as software onto existing cameras and NPUs.NeoSight is offered in three forms: an SDK embedded by NPU makers, a module that attaches to existing cameras and CCTV, and a finished AI camera for drones and robots. Neowise plans to lead with NeoSight into the CCTV, defense and robotics markets, targeting first the areas where darkness has limited operating hours, such as night-time surveillance and reconnaissance, 24-hour unmanned patrols and autonomous indoor flight without lighting.

Neowise developed all three of its core technologies in-house: NeoSight (image restoration and recognition), NeoTwin (3D spatial reconstruction) and NeoSim, a simulation technology that transfers real-world spaces into virtual environments to train and validate autonomous behavior for robots and drones. The site NeoTwin captures becomes the simulator, and the night-time imagery NeoSight restores becomes the training condition. On this foundation, the company's ultimate goal is to build a Physical AI foundation model for the construction and defense sectors. NeoSim already supports Real to Sim and Sim to Real and is applied to indoor autonomous flight; the company also aims to apply NeoSim to training Korea's 520,000 drone warriors and help make the country a drone powerhouse.

Since its founding, Neowise has been selected for TIPS, the flagship program of the Ministry of SMEs and Startups; is carrying out a Republic of Korea Army AX Sprint project and the Air Force Defense Startup Challenge; and has delivered a simulator to the Agency for Defense Development (ADD). It has filed 25 patents, with 8 granted and one PCT international application, and established a U.S. subsidiary in Delaware in October 2025. This month it is engaging U.S. defense, robotics and CCTV customers through the Silicon Valley GTM program of the Korea Institute of Startup & Entrepreneurship Development (KISED). The company targets revenue of more than KRW 400 million in 2026, over KRW 2 billion in 2027 and break-even in 2028.

"The CES Innovation Award is proof that the direction we chose after fifteen pivots has been recognized on the world stage," Shin said. "We will make robots and drones see and understand space as well as people do — night or day, indoors or out — and build a world where darkness and unknown spaces are no longer the limits of machines."
